dhp360:1: Restraint with the eye is good,
dhp360:2: good is restraint with the ear.
dhp360:3: Restraint with the nose is good,
dhp360:4: good is restraint with the tongue.
dhp361:1: Restraint with the body is good,
dhp361:3: Restraint with the heart is good,
dhp361:6: is released from all suffering & stress.
dhp362:4:
content, centered, alone:
he’s what they call
a monk.
dhp363:1: A monk restrained in his speaking,
dhp364:1:
Dhamma his dwelling,
Dhamma his delight,
dhp364:4:
does not fall away
from true Dhamma.
dhp365:1:
Gains:
don’t treat your own with scorn,
dhp365:2: don’t go coveting those of others.
dhp365:3: A monk who covets those of others
dhp366:1: Even if he gets next to nothing,
dhp366:2: he doesn’t treat his gains with scorn.
dhp366:3:
Living purely, untiring:
he’s the one
that the devas praise.
dhp367:1:
For whom, in name & form
in every way,
there’s no sense of mine,
dhp367:3:
& who doesn’t grieve
for what’s not:
dhp368:2: with faith in the Awakened One’s teaching,
dhp368:3:
would attain the good state,
the peaceful state:
dhp369:2: It will take you lightly when bailed.
dhp369:4: you go from there to Unbinding.
dhp370:1:
Cut through five,
let go of five,
dhp370:3: A monk gone past five attachments
dhp370:4: is said to have crossed the flood.
dhp371:1:
Practice jhana, monk,
and don’t be heedless.
dhp371:2:
Don’t take your mind roaming
in sensual strands.
dhp371:3:
Don’t swallow–heedless–
the ball of iron aflame.
dhp372:1:
There’s
no jhana
for one with
no discernment,
dhp372:2:
no discernment
for one with
no jhana.
dhp372:3:
But one with
both jhana
& discernment:
dhp372:4:
he’s on the verge
of Unbinding.
dhp373:1:
A monk with his mind at peace,
going into an empty dwelling,
dhp373:3:
his delight is more
than human.
dhp374:4:
that, for those who know it,
is deathless,
the Deathless.
dhp375:4: restraint in line with the Patimokkha.
dhp376:1: He should associate with admirable friends.
dhp376:6:
he will put an end
to suffering & stress.
dhp377:1:
Shed passion
& aversion, monks–
as a jasmine would,
dhp378:1:
Calmed in body,
calmed in speech,
dhp378:3: having disgorged the baits of the world,
dhp378:4:
a monk is called
thoroughly
calmed.
dhp379:3:
As a self-guarded monk
with guarded self,
mindful,
dhp380:3:
Your own self is
your own guide.
dhp380:4:
Therefore you should
watch over yourself–
dhp380:5: as a trader, a fine steed.
dhp381:1: A monk with a manifold joy,
dhp381:2: with faith in the Awakened One’s teaching,
dhp381:3:
would attain the good state,
the peaceful state:
dhp382:4: like the moon set free from a cloud.
